CP 2050 - The Nature and Development of Science
Credits: 4
The course involves students in the study and reflection within the historical context of the development of science as a
forum to synthesize their learning of various scientific disciplines. The context is provided by a thorough analysis of the
historical and philosophical foundations of scientific knowledge and practice, and its emergency as a distinctly modern
view of the universe. The course addresses National Science Education Standards that call for an understanding of the
history and development of science, as well as its interdisciplinary nature. Note: This course does not fulfill the Liberal
Education Curriculum Domain Science requirement.
Prerequisites
EMS
CP 2070 - Introduction to Forensic Science
Credits: 4
This course is an introduction to forensic chemistry intended for non-science majors. The course examines the many
ways that chemical principles and scientific techniques are applied in modern crime investigation: the chemical
characteristics of fuels and explosives as well as arson-related methods; other ways of identifying criminals through
chemical processes, including blood and bodily fluid analyses, the chemical characteristics found in paints, fibers, hair,
DNA, and fingerprinting; and the chemical properties of drug analysis. Students learn the fundamentals of forensic
science and applications in crime investigation and adjudication.

Credits: 3

stoichiometry, periodicity, bonding and states of matter. Principles are illustrated through demonstrations and study of
descriptive chemistry.

CP 2130 - Principles of Chemistry II
Credits: 3
Continuation of Principles of Chemistry I. Discussion of acid/base and oxidation/reduction reactions, equilibrium,

CP 2400 - Ocean Studies
Credits: 3
This is an introductory oceanography course suitable for students with no prior science background. This course
investigates the world’s oceans from an earth system perspective, emphasizing interactions between spheres (i.e.,
hydrosphere, atmosphere). Topics covered will include the physical and chemical properties of seawater, flow and
transformations of water and energy, and ocean circulation. Students will also study adaptations of marine life and
human societal impacts on the oceans. Learning activities will make use of real-time ocean data accessible via the web.
Note: This course is conducted online.
Prerequisites
Math Proficiency;
CP 2401 - Ocean Studies Lab
Credits: 1
Laboratory course designed to illustrate concepts taught in Ocean Studies (CP 2400
). Laboratory investigations will be both hands-on and web-based, and will include the interpretation of real-time ocean
data.
When Offered:
In conjunction with CP 2400
. Successful completion of Ocean Studies and Ocean Studies Lab satisfies the college Liberal Education Curriculum
requirement for a laboratory science course.

CP 2600 - Environmental Analysis of Long Island
Credits: 4
This is an introductory course that will focus on the study of the natural sciences of Long Island. It includes many
aspects of biology, earth and atmospheric sciences, fundamental principles of chemistry and physics, human population
dynamics, and an appreciation for biological and natural resources. It will always include the consideration of people
and how they have influenced the system under examination. This course will use laboratory, field and a case study
approach to give the students a “hands-on” approach to the fundamental principles of environmental analysis. There
will be an emphasis on laboratory and field methodologies, data analysis, and technical communication within an
interdisciplinary context.
Prerequisites
ECl

11/7/26, 2:10 PM Course Descriptions - SUNY Old Westbury
Credits: 4
An introductory nutrition course suitable for non-science majors. Includes application of nutrition principles to daily
dietary practice. Macro & micronutrients, energy metabolism and balance, weight management and fitness, life cycle
nutrition at different stages of life, and food and the global environment. Major chronic diseases linked to nutrition and
current topics in nutrition will be discussed. Students will complete detailed individual analysis of their diet and will
gain the knowledge and skills needed to achieve a nutritionally healthy lifestyle. Course includes laboratory exercises.
Prerequisites
Math Proficiency;
CP 3230 - Mathematical Methods in the Physical Sciences
Credits: 3
This course covers a variety of essential mathematical concepts and techniques used in chemistry, focusing on
applications to physical problems rather than on deviations and proofs. Topics will include infinite series, complex
functions, differential equations, vector spaces and linear algebra, and Fourier analysis.
Prerequisites
MA 2320
When Offered:
Fall
Note:
This course is crosslisted with PX 3100 Mathematical Methods in Physics

Credits: 3

emphasis on structure, reactions, synthesis, stereochemistry and reaction mechanism.

CP 4490 - Biochemistry for Life Sciences
Credits: 3
One semester survey course designed for life science majors requiring only one semester of biochemistry. We will cover
basic concepts about pH, biological buffers, bioenergetics, nucleotides, amino acids, proteins, enzymes, carbohydrates,
lipids, intermediary metabolism, and molecular biology. This course is not open to Biochemistry majors for credit.
Prerequisites
CP 3310 with a grade of C or better
CP 4510 - Biochemistry I
Credits: 3
Comprehensive coverage of the chemistry and metabolism of biological compounds, including proteins, nucleic acids,
lipids, polysaccharides, and their precursors. Also treats enzyme kinetics, bioenergetics and biosynthesis of important
biomolecules.

dietary practice. Macro & micronutrients, energy metabolism and balance, weight management and fitness, life cycle
nutrition at different stages of life, and food and the global environment. Major chronic diseases linked to nutrition and
current topics in nutrition will be discussed. Students will complete detailed individual analysis of their diet and will
gain the knowledge and skills needed to achieve a nutritionally healthy lifestyle. Course includes laboratory exercises.
Prerequisites
Math Proficiency;

records.title: Mathematical Methods in the Physical Sciences
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
This course covers a variety of essential mathematical concepts and techniques used in chemistry, focusing on
applications to physical problems rather than on deviations and proofs. Topics will include infinite series, complex
functions, differential equations, vector spaces and linear algebra, and Fourier analysis.
Prerequisites
MA 2320
When Offered:
Fall
Note:
This course is crosslisted with PX 3100 Mathematical Methods in Physics

records.title: Organic Chemistry I
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
The first semester of an introductory organic chemistry course. Discussion of major classes of organic compounds, with
emphasis on structure, reactions, synthesis, stereochemistry and reaction mechanism.

Prerequisites
CP 2130 completed with grade of “C” or better
When Offered:
Every Fall.

records.title: Organic Chemistry Lab I
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Designed to illustrate topics of CP 3300. Stresses development of laboratory skills in synthesis, separation and
purification of organic compounds. Emphasizes scientific report writing skills. Four laboratory hours per week.
Prerequisites
CP 2130 and CP 2131 with grades of “C” or better;
When Offered:
In conjunction with CP 3300.

records.title: Organic Chemistry II
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
Continuation of Organic Chemistry I, with discussion of additional major classes of organic compounds.
Prerequisites
CP 3300
When Offered:
Every Spring.

records.title: Organic Chemistry Lab II
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Designed to illustrate topics of CP 3310. Stresses additional synthetic techniques not covered in CP 3302, spectroscopic
methods and qualitative organic analysis. Emphasizes scientific report writing skills. Four laboratory hours per week.

Prerequisites
CP 3302
When Offered:
In conjunction with CP 3310.

records.title: Analytical Chemistry
records.sourceText:
Credits: 5
Study of chemical stoichiometry, homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria, principles of volumetric and gravimetric
analysis, chemical separation methods and spectrophotometry. Includes statistical analysis of data and scientific record-
keeping. Two lectures and one four-hour laboratory per week.
Prerequisites
CP 2130
, CP 2131
completed with grades of “C” or better
When Offered:
Every Fall.

records.title: Inorganic Chemistry
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
Study of inorganic chemistry emphasizing the use of thermodynamic, kinetic and quantum mechanical principles.
Topics include structure, bonding, descriptive chemistry, coordination compounds, group theory, and discussion of
current topics from the literature.
Prerequisites
CP 2130

When Offered:
Periodically.

records.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
An examination of modern synthetic methods, molecular orbital theory, linear free energy relationships, acid‑base
catalysis, neighboring group participation, medium and salt effects, and a detailed consideration of the mechanistic
features of a wide variety of organic reactions.
Prerequisites
CP 3310
;
When Offered:
Periodically.

records.title: Biochemistry for Life Sciences
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
One semester survey course designed for life science majors requiring only one semester of biochemistry. We will cover
basic concepts about pH, biological buffers, bioenergetics, nucleotides, amino acids, proteins, enzymes, carbohydrates,
lipids, intermediary metabolism, and molecular biology. This course is not open to Biochemistry majors for credit.
Prerequisites
CP 3310 with a grade of C or better

records.title: Biochemistry I
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
Comprehensive coverage of the chemistry and metabolism of biological compounds, including proteins, nucleic acids,
lipids, polysaccharides, and their precursors. Also treats enzyme kinetics, bioenergetics and biosynthesis of important
biomolecules.

Prerequisites
CP 3310 with a grade of C or better
When Offered:
Every Fall.

records.title: Biochemistry II
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
Continuation of Biochemistry I, with emphasis on the control of biochemical processes, photosynthesis, replication,
transcription and translation, genetic engineering, ribosomes, and metabolism.
Prerequisites
CP 4510
with a grade of C or better
When Offered:
Every Spring.

records.title: Biochemistry Lab
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Laboratory experiments illustrating current biochemical techniques and reinforcing lecture topics. Four laboratory hours
per week.
When Offered:
In conjunction with CP 4510.

records.title: Forensic Chemistry Techniques
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
This course offers an introduction to the role of chemistry in criminal investigations, with a focus on the principles,
techniques, and methods used to analyze physical evidence in forensic science. Topics include the identification and

analysis of substances like drugs, toxins, and explosives, along with the use of tools such as chromatography and
spectroscopy. Students will explore how forensic chemists aid in solving crimes. The course emphasizes the
foundational principles of analytical chemistry and hands-on experience in forensic analysis and evidence handling. The
prerequisite for CP4600 is successful completion of Analytical Chemistry (CP3400) lectures and labs with a grade of C or
better. The CP4600 is completed over 7 weeks during Term A.
Prerequisites
Analytical Chemistry (CP3400) lectures and labs with a grade of C or better.
When Offered:
Spring Only

records.title: Physical Chemistry I
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
Survey of the basic principles of physical chemistry, with emphasis on thermodynamics, changes of state, solutions,
phase equilibria and kinetic theory.
Prerequisites
CP 2130
completed with grade of “C” or better; MA 2320
completed with a grade of “C” or better, PX 2300
or PX 2100
completed with a grade of “C”or better
When Offered:
Every Fall
Note:
This course is crosslisted with PX 4100 Thermodynamics.

records.title: Physical Chemistry II
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3

Survey of the basic principles of physical chemistry with emphasis on chemical kinetics, quantum mechanics, atomic
and molecular structure.
Prerequisites
CP 2130
completed with a grade of “C” or better; MA 2320
completed with a grade of “C” or better, PX 2300
or PX 2100
completed with a grade of “C” or better
When Offered:
Spring
Note:
This course is cross-listed with PX 4300 Applied Quantum Mechanics

records.title: Physical Chemistry Lab
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Laboratory experiments designed to illustrate the chemical principles underlying thermodynamics, equilibria, surface
and transport properties, chemical kinetics, and spectroscopy. Includes vacuum techniques and use of computers to
acquire and analyze data. Emphasizes scientific report writing in standard format.
When Offered:
In conjunction with CP 4710
.

records.title: Instrumental Analysis
records.sourceText:
Credits: 5
A study of organic and inorganic compounds using instrumental methods of characterization. Synthetic techniques may
include use of inert atmosphere and electrochemical methods. Characterization of compounds may utilize spectroscopy,
GC/MS, LC/MS, electrochemistry, NMR and others. Two lectures and one four-hour laboratory per week. Emphasis on
scientific report writing in standard format.

Prerequisites
CP 3310
, CP 3312
, CP 3400
, with a grade of “C”or better
When Offered:
Every Spring.

records.title: Advanced Topics in Chemistry
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
One‑semester lecture course covering selected topics of current importance to chemists. Course content may include
such topics as spectroscopy, radiation chemistry, electricity and magnetism, molecular orbital theory, group theory and
new instrumental techniques.
Prerequisites
Permission of the Instructor
When Offered:
Periodically.

records.title: Research
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2‑4
Research project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. Each project includes a survey of the
appropriate original literature, a theoretical or experimental investigation, and a comprehensive report of the results.
Open only to students accepted as research trainees sponsored by a member of the Chemistry and Physics faculty.
Prerequisites
Permission of the Chemistry/Physics faculty
When Offered:
Every semester. Grading will be CR/NC.

records.title: Seminar I
records.sourceText:
Credits: 1
Capstone course in which the student integrates coursework in the sub-disciplines to discuss topics of current interest in
the profession. Includes instruction in library resources and on-line searching, scientific writing, ethics workshops and
oral presentations. Students choose a supervisor and seminar topic and submit a draft written report. Attendance at
Science Seminar Series is required.
Prerequisites
Senior Standing or Permission of the Instructor
When Offered:
Every Fall.

records.title: Seminar II
records.sourceText:
Credits: 1
Continuation of CP 5920
. Emphasis on producing paper in American Chemical Society format. Attendance at Science Seminar Series is required.
Prerequisites
CP 5920
When Offered:
Every Spring.

records.title: Independent Study in Chemistry/Physics
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2-4
An academic project other than laboratory research carried out under the supervision of a faculty member.
Prerequisites
Permission of the Chemistry/Physics faculty

When Offered:
Every semester.
